title: Run a Microsoft Copilot readiness check before you assign licenses
problem: Teams buy Copilot licenses and assign them before prerequisites (apps, update channel, identity, data access) are in place, leading to a poor first impression.
steps: Confirm users have a qualifying Microsoft 365 base license (Copilot isn't available with device-based licensing for Microsoft 365 Apps) and Microsoft 365 Apps on Current Channel or Monthly Enterprise Channel.
Confirm users have a Microsoft Entra ID account, an Exchange Online mailbox (for mail/calendar/meeting grounding) and OneDrive (needed for some features).

Network: allow the whole *.cloud.microsoft domain (including copilot.cloud.microsoft) and full WebSocket Secure (WSS) connectivity to *.office.com and *.cloud.microsoft; avoid TLS inspection on that traffic.
Review oversharing risk in SharePoint before broad rollout (see the oversharing recipes).
Assign licenses to a pilot group first and validate users with the Copilot License Details diagnostic.
pitfalls: Since July 2026 (version 2606) Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel is unified with Monthly Enterprise Channel, so SAEC devices get the MEC experience — but reports may still show SAEC.
Proxies or TLS inspection that break WebSockets make Copilot in apps fail.
done_when: Every pilot user has a qualifying base license, an Entra ID account, an Exchange Online mailbox and OneDrive.
Pilot devices report Microsoft 365 Apps on Current Channel or Monthly Enterprise Channel.
Your network team has confirmed *.cloud.microsoft is allowed in full and WSS traffic is not broken by TLS inspection.
The Copilot License Details diagnostic shows no blocking issues for your pilot users.

sources.title: Microsoft Copilot requirements
Microsoft Copilot adoption guide and overview for IT admins
Channel unification: Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel to Monthly Enterprise Channel

title: Assign Copilot licenses to a pilot group with group-based licensing
problem: Manually assigning Copilot licenses per user does not scale and is hard to audit.
steps: Create a security group, e.g. 'SG-Copilot-Pilot' (no nested groups — they aren't supported).

Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses > Assign licenses: pick the group and the Microsoft Copilot subscription (group-based licensing is managed in the Microsoft 365 admin center, not the Entra admin center).
Add pilot users to the group; licenses are applied automatically.
Monitor errors under Billing > Licenses > the product > Errors & issues.
pitfalls: Group-based licensing requires Microsoft Entra ID P1 or Office 365 E3 or higher.
Removing a user from the group removes the license — when moving users, add to the new group first, then remove from the old one.
done_when: The pilot security group shows the Microsoft Copilot license under Billing > Licenses with no nested groups inside it.
A newly added test user receives the license automatically, without a manual assignment.
Errors & issues for the product is empty, or every listed error has an owner.

sources.title: Assign or unassign licenses to a group in the Microsoft 365 admin center
Manage licenses (Microsoft Learn training)

title: Assign a Microsoft Copilot license to a user with Microsoft Graph PowerShell
problem: You need to script license assignment for a list of users.
steps: Connect: `Connect-MgGraph -Scopes 'User.ReadWrite.All','Organization.Read.All'`
Find the SKU: `Get-MgSubscribedSku | Select SkuPartNumber, SkuId`
Set a usage location if missing: `Update-MgUser -UserId user@contoso.com -UsageLocation SE`
Assign: `Set-MgUserLicense -UserId user@contoso.com -AddLicenses @{SkuId='<SkuId>'} -RemoveLicenses @()`
pitfalls: Licenses cannot be assigned without UsageLocation.
Look up the SkuPartNumber in your tenant rather than hard-coding it.
done_when: `Get-MgUserLicenseDetail -UserId <user>` lists the Copilot SKU for every user in your list.
Every target user has a UsageLocation set.
Your script reads the SkuId from Get-MgSubscribedSku instead of a hard-coded value.

sources.title: Assign licenses with Microsoft Graph PowerShell
Set-MgUserLicense

title: Plan adoption with the Microsoft Copilot adoption resources
problem: Licenses get assigned but usage stays low because nobody planned training or champions.
steps: Pick 3–5 business scenarios per department (meeting recap, email drafting, document summary).
Recruit a champions group and give them early access.
Use the Copilot Dashboard in Viva Insights to track readiness, adoption and impact (no paid Viva Insights license needed).
Run monthly 'show and tell' sessions and collect prompts that work.
pitfalls: Measuring only license count, not active usage.
Skipping manager enablement — managers drive adoption.
Group-level (scoped) data in the Copilot Dashboard requires at least 50 Copilot or Viva Insights licenses; smaller tenants get tenant-level data.
done_when: Each pilot department has 3–5 named scenarios written down.
A champions group exists, has early access and a recurring session in the calendar.
Someone owns the Copilot Dashboard in Viva Insights and reviews it on a fixed schedule.

sources.title: Microsoft Copilot adoption
Connect to the Copilot Dashboard

title: Decide whether Copilot can use web content (web search)
problem: Security asks whether prompts can be sent to Bing for web grounding and wants a control.
steps: Review how web search works: Copilot sends short generated search queries to Bing — not the full prompt, files or Entra identity (very short prompts can be sent as-is).
Control it with the 'Allow web search in Copilot' policy in Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365: enabled, disabled, or disabled in Work mode but enabled in Web mode and Copilot Chat.
For finer control, a Purview DLP rule can block web search only when prompts contain sensitive information types.
Document the decision and communicate it to users.
pitfalls: Turning off web search reduces answer quality for public-information questions.
Policies are applied via Cloud Policy and can take time to reach clients.
The DPA and EU Data Boundary don't apply to the generated Bing queries.
done_when: The 'Allow web search in Copilot' policy is set to the value you chose, in the Cloud Policy service, and assigned to the right groups.
The decision (and any DLP rule for sensitive prompts) is documented and has been shared with users.

sources.title: Manage web search in Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat
DLP for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat

title: Make Copilot in Teams meetings work: transcription and recording policies
problem: Users can't use Copilot in meetings, or Copilot disappears after the meeting.
steps: Transcription must be allowed (Teams meeting policy, -AllowTranscription) and a transcript started for Copilot to work after the meeting.
Organizers choose 'During and after the meeting', 'Only during the meeting' or 'Off' in meeting options.
Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > Recording & transcription > Copilot: On, On with saved transcript required (default), On with transcript saved by default, or Off.
PowerShell: `Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy> -Copilot EnabledWithTranscriptDefaultOn`
pitfalls: 'Only during the meeting' means no post-meeting recap — users think Copilot is broken.
The Copilot default comes from the organizer's meeting policy; transcription can be started by any participant whose own policy allows it.
Copilot isn't available in end-to-end encrypted meetings.
done_when: The meeting policy for pilot users allows transcription and has the Copilot setting you chose.
In a test meeting where a transcript was started, Copilot can still be used on that meeting after it ends.

sources.title: Manage Microsoft Copilot in Teams meetings and events

title: Require phishing-resistant MFA for users accessing Microsoft Copilot
problem: Copilot can surface a lot of data quickly, so a compromised account is more dangerous. You want stronger authentication for licensed users.
steps: Entra admin center > Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies > New policy.
Users: include the Copilot license group; exclude break-glass accounts.
Target resources: Office 365 (the Office 365 app group includes Enterprise Copilot Platform).
Grant: Require authentication strength > Phishing-resistant MFA.
Start in Report-only, review sign-in logs, then turn On.
pitfalls: Don't lock out break-glass accounts — always exclude them.
Users without a phishing-resistant method (passkey/FIDO2, Windows Hello for Business, certificate-based authentication or macOS Platform SSO) will be blocked once enforced.
done_when: A Conditional Access policy targets Office 365 for the Copilot license group with the Phishing-resistant MFA authentication strength.
Break-glass accounts are excluded.
Report-only results were reviewed in the sign-in logs and the policy is now On.

sources.title: Conditional Access authentication strengths
Apps included in the Office 365 app group

troubleshooting.symptom: A user in the Copilot license group is blocked after the policy is turned On.
troubleshooting.cause: They have no registered method that satisfies the Phishing-resistant MFA authentication strength.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the sign-in event's Conditional Access tab to confirm which policy blocked it, then have the user register a phishing-resistant method (for example a passkey). A Temporary Access Pass can be used to bootstrap that registration.

troubleshooting.symptom: Break-glass accounts are prompted or blocked by the policy.
troubleshooting.fix: The exclusion is missing or points at the wrong group. Exclude the emergency access group, then test sign-in with one of those accounts.

rollback: Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies: set the policy to Report-only (or Off) instead of deleting it.
Confirm in the sign-in logs that the affected users can sign in again.
Register phishing-resistant methods for the users who were blocked, review the report-only results again, then turn the policy back On.

title: Roll out AI-related Conditional Access policies in report-only mode
problem: A new policy for AI apps could block access for thousands of users if it's wrong.
steps: Create the policy with state 'Report-only'.
Wait 1–2 weeks and review the policy impact view (no Log Analytics needed) or the Conditional Access insights and reporting workbook.
Use the What If tool for edge cases (guests, service accounts).
Switch to On during a maintenance window.
pitfalls: The insights and reporting workbook needs sign-in logs streamed to a Log Analytics workspace.
Report-only policies that require a compliant device can prompt users on macOS, iOS and Android to pick a device certificate — exclude those platforms from report-only device compliance policies.
done_when: The policy has run in Report-only for at least 1–2 weeks and you have reviewed its impact.
What If has been run for guests and service accounts, with the result recorded.
The policy was switched to On in an agreed maintenance window.

sources.title: Conditional Access report-only mode
Conditional Access insights and reporting workbook

title: Require a compliant or hybrid-joined device for Microsoft 365 (and Copilot)
problem: You don't want Copilot answers with sensitive data ending up on unmanaged personal devices.
steps: Entra admin center > Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies > New policy targeting the Copilot users group.
Target resources: Office 365.
Grant: Require device to be marked as compliant OR Require Microsoft Entra hybrid joined device (Require one of the selected controls).
Exclude break-glass accounts (and Directory Synchronization Accounts if you sync); start in report-only.
pitfalls: Unmanaged browsers on personal devices will be blocked — consider app-enforced restrictions instead for web access.
Device compliance requires the device to be enrolled in Intune (or a supported compliance partner).
In report-only, compliant-device policies can prompt macOS, iOS and Android users for a device certificate — exclude those platforms while testing.
done_when: The policy targets Office 365 for the Copilot users group and grants access with 'Require one of the selected controls' (compliant OR hybrid joined).
Break-glass accounts and, if you sync, the Directory Synchronization Accounts are excluded.
Report-only results show no unexpected blocks for managed devices.

sources.title: Require a compliant device, hybrid joined device or MFA
Conditional Access report-only mode

troubleshooting.symptom: Users on personal devices lose browser access to Office 365.
troubleshooting.cause: Unmanaged devices can't satisfy compliant or Entra hybrid joined.
troubleshooting.fix: Expected by design. For web access from unmanaged devices, use app-enforced restrictions instead of widening the policy.

troubleshooting.symptom: A device the user considers managed is treated as noncompliant.
troubleshooting.cause: It isn't enrolled in Intune (or a supported compliance partner), or compliance hasn't been evaluated yet.
troubleshooting.fix: Check enrollment and compliance state in Intune before excluding anyone.

troubleshooting.symptom: macOS, iOS or Android users get a device certificate prompt while the policy is in Report-only.
troubleshooting.fix: Exclude those platforms from the policy during testing.

rollback: Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies: open the compliant-device policy and set Enable policy to Report-only (keeps impact data) or Off. Don't delete it, so the configuration is kept.
Confirm in the sign-in logs (Conditional Access tab on the affected events) that the policy no longer applies and sign-ins succeed.
Fix enrollment/compliance for the affected devices, then switch back to On.

title: Block legacy authentication before you scale AI
problem: Legacy protocols can't do MFA, undermining every AI security control you add.
steps: Entra admin center > Entra ID > Monitoring & health > Sign-in logs: add the Client app column and filter on the legacy authentication protocols (check the non-interactive sign-ins tab too).

Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies > New policy: All users (exclude break-glass accounts), Target resources: All resources, Conditions > Client apps: only Exchange ActiveSync clients and Other clients.
Grant: Block access. Start in Report-only, then switch to On.
pitfalls: Old multifunction printers and scripts using SMTP AUTH break — inventory them first.
Without Conditional Access licenses (Entra ID P1), use security defaults to block legacy authentication instead.
done_when: Sign-in logs (interactive and non-interactive) show no remaining legacy-protocol sign-ins you still need.
A policy for All users / All resources, client apps Exchange ActiveSync + Other clients, Block access, is On with break-glass excluded.

sources.title: Block legacy authentication with Conditional Access

troubleshooting.symptom: A multifunction printer, scanner or script stops sending mail once the policy is On.
troubleshooting.cause: It authenticates with SMTP AUTH or another legacy protocol, which the policy now blocks.
troubleshooting.fix: Find it in the sign-in logs (Client app column, interactive and non-interactive tabs), then move it to an option that supports modern authentication. Avoid a permanent exclusion: it reopens the gap the policy closes.

troubleshooting.symptom: Report-only results show legacy sign-ins you can't attribute.
troubleshooting.fix: Open the sign-in event and check the Report-only tab for which policy would have applied, and the user, app and IP details for the source. Resolve those before switching to On.

rollback: Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies: open the policy and set Enable policy to Report-only (keeps visibility) or Off. Don't delete it, so the configuration is kept.
Confirm in the sign-in logs that the affected sign-ins succeed again.
Fix or replace the client that depended on legacy authentication, then switch the policy back to On.

title: Set sign-in frequency for high-risk Copilot users
problem: Executives with broad data access stay signed in for weeks on shared or traveling devices.
steps: Policy 1: Conditional Access policy for the exec group targeting Office 365; Session: Sign-in frequency, e.g. every 12 hours.

Policy 2 (separate): Persistent browser session = Never persistent. This control requires the policy to target All resources, so it can't live in the Office 365 policy — scope it with a device filter or to unmanaged devices.
Turn off 'Remember MFA on trusted devices' before using sign-in frequency to avoid unexpected prompts.
pitfalls: Too frequent prompts cause MFA fatigue — balance with phishing-resistant methods.
done_when: The exec group has a sign-in frequency policy on Office 365.
A separate policy sets Never persistent browser session, scoped with a device filter or to unmanaged devices.
'Remember MFA on trusted devices' is off.

sources.title: Conditional Access adaptive session lifetime
Configure adaptive session lifetime policies

troubleshooting.symptom: Users get more MFA prompts than the configured frequency suggests.
troubleshooting.cause: 'Remember MFA on trusted devices' is still on alongside sign-in frequency.
troubleshooting.fix: Turn it off, as in the steps.

troubleshooting.symptom: The Never persistent browser session control can't be saved in the Office 365 policy.
troubleshooting.cause: That control requires the policy to target All resources.
troubleshooting.fix: Keep it in a separate All resources policy scoped with a device filter or to unmanaged devices.

troubleshooting.symptom: Complaints about prompt fatigue.
troubleshooting.fix: Lengthen the interval and move users to phishing-resistant methods rather than removing the control.

rollback: Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies: open Policy 1 (sign-in frequency) and/or Policy 2 (persistent browser session), one at a time and set Enable policy to Report-only (keeps impact data) or Off. Don't delete it, so the configuration is kept.
Confirm in the sign-in logs (Conditional Access tab on the affected events) that the policy no longer applies and sign-ins succeed.
Adjust the interval or scope, then switch back to On.

title: Block risky sign-ins and require password change for high user risk
problem: An attacker with a stolen session could use Copilot to search all accessible data quickly.
steps: Requires Microsoft Entra ID P2 (ID Protection).
Policy 1 — sign-in risk: All users, All resources, Sign-in risk High and Medium > Grant: Require authentication strength (Multifactor authentication), Session: Sign-in frequency Every time.
Policy 2 — user risk: All users, All resources, User risk High > Grant: Require risk remediation (authentication strength and sign-in frequency Every time are applied automatically).
Exclude break-glass accounts, start in report-only, then review the Risky users report weekly.
pitfalls: Risk policies need P2 licenses for covered users.
Users who aren't registered for MFA are blocked on risky sign-ins (AADSTS53004) — drive MFA registration first.
done_when: The tenant has Entra ID P2, and two separate policies exist: one for sign-in risk (High, Medium) and one for user risk (High).
Break-glass accounts are excluded from both, and both have been reviewed in report-only before being turned On.
Someone owns a weekly review of the Risky users report.

sources.title: Require MFA for elevated sign-in risk
Require risk remediation for elevated user risk

troubleshooting.symptom: Risky sign-ins fail with AADSTS53004.
troubleshooting.cause: The user isn't registered for MFA, so the risk policy can't be satisfied.
troubleshooting.fix: Drive MFA registration before switching the policies On; check registration for users flagged in Report-only.

troubleshooting.symptom: Policies don't evaluate risk for some users.
troubleshooting.cause: Risk policies require Entra ID P2 for covered users.
troubleshooting.fix: Verify licensing for the users in scope.

troubleshooting.symptom: High-risk users are repeatedly prompted.
troubleshooting.fix: Expected: Require risk remediation adds sign-in frequency Every time. Review the Risky users report and remediate or dismiss risk.

rollback: Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies: open the sign-in risk and/or user risk policy (roll back one at a time) and set Enable policy to Report-only (keeps impact data) or Off. Don't delete it, so the configuration is kept.
Confirm in the sign-in logs (Conditional Access tab on the affected events) that the policy no longer applies and sign-ins succeed.
Resolve registration or licensing gaps, then return to On.

title: Keep break-glass accounts out of every AI-era CA policy
problem: Rapid policy changes for AI raise the risk of tenant lockout.
steps: Create two cloud-only emergency access accounts with a permanent Global Administrator assignment.

Register a phishing-resistant method that differs from your normal admin accounts — passkey (FIDO2) is recommended, certificate-based authentication is an alternative. This also satisfies mandatory MFA.
Put them in a dedicated group (e.g. EmergencyAccess) and exclude it from every Conditional Access policy that blocks or restricts sign-in (report-only policies don't need the exclusion).
Alert on every sign-in and audit event for these accounts (Azure Monitor/Log Analytics).
Test sign-in at least every 90 days (e.g. quarterly).
pitfalls: Don't tie them to a single person's phone for MFA — store FIDO2 keys securely in separate locations.
done_when: Two cloud-only emergency accounts exist with a permanent Global Administrator assignment and a phishing-resistant method that differs from your normal admins.
Their group is excluded from every enforced policy that blocks or restricts sign-in.
Sign-ins by these accounts trigger an alert, and the last test sign-in is less than 90 days old.

sources.title: Manage emergency access accounts in Microsoft Entra ID

troubleshooting.symptom: An emergency access account is blocked or challenged during the periodic test sign-in.
troubleshooting.cause: A Conditional Access policy that blocks or restricts sign-in doesn't exclude the EmergencyAccess group.
troubleshooting.fix: Open the failed sign-in event, check the Conditional Access tab for the applied policy, and add the group exclusion to it. Re-test.

troubleshooting.symptom: The registered passkey or certificate can't be found or used when you need it.
troubleshooting.fix: Keep the FIDO2 keys for the two accounts in separate secure locations, not on one person's phone, and include method checks in the 90-day test.

troubleshooting.symptom: No alert fires for a test sign-in.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the Azure Monitor/Log Analytics alert rule covers both accounts and both sign-in and audit events; treat a silent test as a failed control.

rollback: Don't remove the accounts or their Global Administrator assignment as a 'rollback'; they are the rollback for every other identity change.
If a new exclusion or alert change causes issues, revert that single change and repeat the test sign-in to confirm access and alerting both work.

title: Deploy Microsoft 365 Apps on Current or Monthly Enterprise Channel with Intune
problem: Copilot features arrive late or not at all on devices on older Microsoft 365 Apps builds or the wrong update channel.
steps: Intune admin center > Apps > All Apps > Create > Microsoft 365 Apps: Windows 10 and later.
Choose the update channel: Current Channel or Monthly Enterprise Channel.
Assign to the Copilot pilot device/user group.
Verify version with the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center inventory.
pitfalls: Changing channel on existing installs may require a separate policy (Office cloud policy or administrative template) — avoid conflicting settings catalog policies, which can trigger reinstalls.
Since version 2606 (July 2026) Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel devices receive the Monthly Enterprise Channel experience, but some reports still show SAEC.
done_when: A Microsoft 365 Apps app in Intune with Current Channel or Monthly Enterprise Channel is assigned to the pilot group.
The Microsoft 365 Apps admin center inventory shows pilot devices on the chosen channel.

sources.title: Add Microsoft 365 Apps to Windows devices with Intune
Overview of update channels for Microsoft 365 Apps
Channel unification: SAEC to MEC

title: Create a Windows compliance policy that CA can rely on
problem: Device-based Conditional Access is meaningless if compliance policies are weak.
steps: Intune > Devices > Compliance > Create policy > Windows 10 and later.
Require BitLocker, Secure Boot, a minimum OS version, and Microsoft Defender Antimalware.
Optionally require the device to be at or under a machine risk score from Defender for Endpoint.
Set actions for noncompliance (Mark device noncompliant after a grace period).
pitfalls: Newly enrolled devices may appear noncompliant until first evaluation — use a grace period.
BitLocker and Secure Boot are measured via Device Health Attestation at boot — a reboot is needed after encryption before the device shows compliant.
done_when: A Windows compliance policy requiring BitLocker, Secure Boot, a minimum OS version and Defender Antimalware is assigned.
Noncompliance actions with a grace period are set.
Test devices report Compliant in Intune before any Conditional Access policy relies on the result.

sources.title: Create a compliance policy in Intune
Windows compliance settings in Intune

troubleshooting.symptom: Newly enrolled devices show noncompliant.
troubleshooting.cause: They haven't completed first evaluation.
troubleshooting.fix: Use a grace period in Actions for noncompliance and wait for the next check-in.

troubleshooting.symptom: BitLocker or Secure Boot reported noncompliant on an encrypted device.
troubleshooting.cause: Device Health Attestation measures them at boot.
troubleshooting.fix: Reboot after encryption, then re-check compliance.

troubleshooting.symptom: Devices fail on machine risk score.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the device in Defender for Endpoint; resolve the risk rather than loosening the threshold.

rollback: If compliance-based Conditional Access blocks users, set that CA policy to Report-only first.
Then extend the grace period, relax the failing setting, or remove the assignment for the affected group; avoid deleting the policy.
Confirm device compliance state in Intune updates after the next check-in.

title: Protect Copilot on iOS/Android with app protection policies
problem: Users want Copilot and Microsoft 365 apps on personal phones without enrolling them.
steps: Intune > Apps > App protection policies > Create (iOS/iPadOS and Android).
Target the Microsoft Copilot app (formerly the Microsoft 365 Copilot app) and the Microsoft 365 apps (Outlook, Teams, Word, etc.).
Data protection: restrict cut/copy/paste to policy-managed apps, block save to personal storage.
Pair with a Conditional Access policy granting 'Require app protection policy' (or approved client app) for iOS/Android.
pitfalls: Only apps that integrate the Intune SDK/are listed as protected apps are covered — check the protected apps list.
Devices must be registered in Microsoft Entra ID (via Authenticator or Company Portal) for the CA grant to work.
done_when: iOS/iPadOS and Android app protection policies cover the Microsoft Copilot app and the Microsoft 365 apps your users run.
Copy/paste to unmanaged apps and saving to personal storage are blocked on a test phone.
A Conditional Access policy requires app protection (or an approved client app) on iOS/Android.

sources.title: App protection policies overview
Microsoft Intune protected apps
Require approved client apps or app protection policy

troubleshooting.symptom: Policy doesn't apply to an app.
troubleshooting.cause: The app doesn't integrate the Intune SDK or isn't on the protected apps list.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the protected apps list; unsupported apps can't be targeted.

troubleshooting.symptom: iOS/Android users are blocked by the 'Require app protection policy' CA grant.
troubleshooting.cause: The device isn't registered in Entra ID via Authenticator or Company Portal.
troubleshooting.fix: Have users install the broker app and register, then retry.

troubleshooting.symptom: Users can't paste into personal apps or save to personal storage.
troubleshooting.fix: Expected from the data protection settings; adjust only if the business case requires it.

rollback: Set the paired Conditional Access policy to Report-only or Off first, so access isn't blocked.
Then remove the group assignment from the app protection policy (or relax the data protection setting) instead of deleting it.
Confirm on a test device that the app re-checks in and the restriction is gone.

title: Manage the Copilot experience on Windows devices
problem: Copilot on Windows changes frequently and admins need to control what users see.
steps: Entra users get the Microsoft Copilot app (previously the Microsoft 365 app) pinned; licensed users can switch between Work and Web.

Set what the Copilot key (or Win+C) opens with the WindowsAI CSP `./User/Vendor/MSFT/Policy/Config/WindowsAI/SetCopilotHardwareKey` (GPO: Windows Components > Windows Copilot > Set Copilot Hardware Key).
Block the consumer Copilot app (package MICROSOFT.COPILOT) with AppLocker, or remove it per device; deploy the apps you want with Intune per group.
Communicate to users what the Copilot key opens in your tenant.
pitfalls: The legacy 'Turn off Windows Copilot' policy (TurnOffWindowsCopilot) is slated for deprecation — Microsoft recommends AppLocker instead.
done_when: The Copilot key (or Win+C) opens the app you chose on a test device.
The consumer Copilot app is blocked or removed where you decided it should be.
Users have been told what the key opens.

sources.title: Manage Copilot on Windows

title: Keep AI-ready devices current with Windows Autopatch
problem: Copilot and security features depend on current Windows and Office builds.
steps: Register devices in Windows Autopatch and organize them with Autopatch groups and update rings.
Include Microsoft 365 Apps updates (Autopatch targets Monthly Enterprise Channel), plus Edge and Teams.
Monitor Intune update reports for devices falling behind.
pitfalls: Autopatch features require Business Premium, A3+, E3+ or F3 licenses — check eligibility first.
done_when: Devices are registered in Windows Autopatch and appear in your Autopatch groups.
Microsoft 365 Apps, Edge and Teams updates are included.
Someone checks the Intune update reports for devices falling behind on a fixed schedule.

sources.title: What is Windows Autopatch?

title: Control generative AI in Microsoft Edge with Intune settings catalog
problem: You want enterprise data protection in the browser and to manage Copilot in the Edge sidebar.
steps: Intune > Devices > Configuration > Create > New policy > Windows 10 and later > Settings catalog, then search for Microsoft Edge.
Configure the Copilot policies you decided on, e.g. EdgeCopilotEnabled, Microsoft365CopilotChatIconEnabled (toolbar icon) and EdgeEntraCopilotPageContext (page context for Entra profiles).
Assign to device groups and verify at edge://policy.
pitfalls: Policy names change between Edge versions — always check the current Edge policy reference.
done_when: A settings catalog policy with your chosen Edge Copilot settings is assigned to device groups.
edge://policy on a test device lists the policies with status OK.

sources.title: Microsoft Edge browser policy documentation
Configure Microsoft Edge with Intune

troubleshooting.symptom: A configured setting doesn't show up at edge://policy.
troubleshooting.cause: The device hasn't synced, isn't in the assigned device group, or the policy name changed in the Edge version in use.
troubleshooting.fix: Check assignment and sync, then compare against the current Edge policy reference.

troubleshooting.symptom: edge://policy shows an error for a policy.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the value and the supported Edge version in the Edge policy reference.

rollback: Remove the specific Copilot setting from the Settings catalog profile (or unassign the device group); don't delete the whole profile if it carries other settings.
Sync the device and confirm at edge://policy that the setting is gone.

category: Purview, DLP & data security for Copilot
title: Find oversharing before Copilot does: data security posture for AI
problem: Copilot respects permissions, so content shared with 'Everyone' becomes discoverable through Copilot.
steps: Open Microsoft Purview > Data Security Posture Management (DSPM, or DSPM for AI (classic)).
Review the default weekly data risk assessment for oversharing, or create a custom data risk assessment for specific sites.
Review top sites with sensitive content shared broadly.
Remediate: restrict access, apply labels, or use Restricted Content Discovery.
pitfalls: Assessment results are a snapshot — rerun after remediation.
done_when: You have reviewed the latest oversharing data risk assessment (default or custom).
Each top site with broadly shared sensitive content has an owner and a remediation decision (restrict, label or Restricted Content Discovery).
The assessment has been run again after remediation.

sources.title: Microsoft Purview data security and compliance protections for generative AI apps
Purview for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat

category: Purview, DLP & data security for Copilot
title: Hide specific sites from Copilot with Restricted Content Discovery
problem: A few sensitive sites should not be surfaced by Copilot or org-wide search.
steps: Requires a Microsoft Copilot license in the tenant and SharePoint Advanced Management (included with Microsoft Copilot or as an add-on).
SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > select the site > Settings > turn on 'Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot' > Save.
Or PowerShell: `Connect-SPOService -Url https://contoso-admin.sharepoint.com` then `Set-SPOSite -Identity <siteUrl> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true`
Verify after reindexing (can take time for large sites).
pitfalls: Users with access can still open the site directly — it's not a permission change.
Works only on SharePoint sites, not OneDrive, and also hides Copilot entry points on the site.
Use it selectively — overuse reduces what search and Copilot can find.
done_when: The selected sites show 'Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot' as on (or RestrictContentOrgWideSearch is $true).

category: Purview, DLP & data security for Copilot
title: Make Copilot respect sensitivity labels and encryption
problem: You need to know how labeled and encrypted content is handled in Copilot responses.
steps: Publish sensitivity labels to users.
Copilot applies the highest-priority label of referenced content to new content in supported scenarios (and it replaces a lower-priority manual label).
For encrypted content, Copilot needs the user to have both EXTRACT and VIEW usage rights.
To stop Copilot summarizing files at rest, use labels that apply encryption without the EXTRACT right. Test with a pilot user.
pitfalls: Content without the EXTRACT right won't be summarized — expected behavior, not a bug.
Container labels (sites, teams) aren't inherited by items, so Copilot won't show them for that content.
done_when: Sensitivity labels are published to the pilot users.
A pilot test confirms how Copilot handles a file with an encryption label that lacks the EXTRACT right, and the result matches your intent.

You can't combine sensitive information types and sensitivity labels in the same rule — create separate rules.

title: Move users off SMS and voice MFA before Microsoft-provided SMS and voice retire on 1 February 2027
problem: Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication retires on 1 February 2027 (1 July 2027 for Global Administrators and external users). After that date, users whose only MFA method is SMS or voice get a blocking prompt to register a passkey before they can sign in.
steps: Find who still depends on SMS or voice: run the PowerShell script or the SMS/voice usage analyzer linked from Microsoft's retirement guide (needs Global Reader, Authentication Policy Administrator or Security Reader).
Put those users in a security group so every following step can target them.

Entra admin center > Entra ID > (Security >) Authentication methods > Policies: make sure Passkey (FIDO2) is enabled and that the group is in scope. Synced passkeys and device-bound passkeys (Microsoft Authenticator, FIDO2 keys, Windows) are both supported.

Entra ID > Authentication methods > Registration campaign: set State to Microsoft managed and target the group, so users are nudged to register a passkey the next time they complete MFA. Choose Enabled instead if you need to control the targeted method or how often users can snooze.

Only for user segments with a documented regulatory or operational need, pick a telephony provider in Microsoft Security Store (selectable from 30 October 2026) and pilot it. Microsoft recommends finishing setup at least 4 weeks before 1 February 2027.

Tell users what is coming: since 1 September 2026, users enabled for SMS or voice are auto-enabled for passkeys and prompted to register one at MFA sign-in. They can skip the prompt until their retirement date, but not after it.
Do Global Administrators first even though their deadline is later: your most privileged accounts should be on phishing-resistant MFA anyway.
pitfalls: Self-service password reset is in scope too: native SMS and voice retire across Microsoft Entra, including SSPR.
Internal guest users follow the 1 February 2027 date. Only Global Administrators and external users get until 1 July 2027.

The temporary opt-out (setting passkeyDynamicMigration in the authentication methods policy via Microsoft Graph) only delays the automatic passkey enablement and registration campaign. There is no opt-out from enforcement.

B2B guests are affected as well: passkey support for B2B users is rolling out from late October 2026 (MC1459133), and guests enabled for SMS or voice are auto-enabled for all passkey types. Excluding them from the passkey policy alone doesn't stop that; move them off SMS and voice instead.
done_when: You have a list (and a security group) of every user who still relies only on SMS or voice.
Passkey (FIDO2) is enabled for that group and a registration campaign targets it.
Global Administrators are on phishing-resistant methods, and users have been told about the 1 February 2027 deadline.

title: Check the Microsoft-managed 'Require risk remediation for high-risk users' policy that just switched on
problem: In Entra ID P2 tenants Microsoft created a managed Conditional Access policy in report-only mode the week of 28 September 2026. If nobody touched it, it switched to On automatically the week of 28 October 2026, so high-risk users are now forced to self-remediate.
steps: Entra admin center > Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies: open 'Require risk remediation for high-risk users' (Microsoft-managed) and note the security group that was created with it.
Open the Policy impact tab to see which sign-ins the policy affected while it was in report-only.
Exclude your break-glass/emergency access accounts, or narrow the scope by changing the membership of the policy's security group.
Make sure the users in scope are registered for MFA so they can self-remediate. In hybrid tenants, self-remediation by secure password change relies on password hash sync.
Decide on the state: leave it On, or set it to Off if you already run your own user-risk policy. If you need more changes than exclusions and state, use Duplicate and build your own copy.
Afterwards, check Entra ID > Monitoring & health > Sign-in logs, filtered on Conditional Access, for users stuck in remediation.
pitfalls: It remediates user risk, not sign-in risk.
Precedence: Require risk remediation overrides Require password change, and Block overrides all others. Check how it overlaps with your existing risk policies.
The policy isn't supported for external and guest users.
Microsoft-managed policies can't be renamed or deleted, only scoped (exclusions) and switched On or Off.
The grant controls automatically add authentication strength and sign-in frequency 'Every time', so after their sessions are revoked users have to sign in again.
done_when: You know the state and the security group of the Microsoft-managed 'Require risk remediation for high-risk users' policy.
Break-glass accounts are excluded.
You have made a deliberate decision to keep it On or turn it Off, and the sign-in logs show no users stuck in remediation.

troubleshooting.symptom: Users are stuck in remediation and can't sign in.
troubleshooting.cause: They aren't registered for MFA, or (hybrid) password hash sync isn't enabled, so secure password change can't complete.
troubleshooting.fix: Find them in the sign-in logs filtered on Conditional Access, drive MFA registration, check PHS, or have an admin remediate the user risk.

troubleshooting.symptom: Guest or external users hit unexpected results.
troubleshooting.cause: The policy isn't supported for external and guest users.
troubleshooting.fix: Narrow scope via the policy's security group membership.

troubleshooting.symptom: A different grant than expected is enforced.
troubleshooting.cause: Precedence: Block overrides all, and Require risk remediation overrides Require password change.
troubleshooting.fix: Review overlap with your own user-risk policies; if you run one, set the managed policy to Off.

title: Stop 'access denied' for external users as SharePoint one-time passcode retires
problem: SharePoint Online one-time passcode (OTP) authentication began retiring in commercial tenants in mid-October 2026, and the retirement should be complete by the end of November 2026. External users without a matching Entra B2B guest account then get 'access denied' on previously shared 'Specific people' links.
steps: Find who is affected: run the sharing report on key sites (Settings > Site usage > Shared with external users > Run report) or in OneDrive, and use sharing auditing in the audit log. Microsoft Graph Data Connect site sharing reports work at larger scale.
Create the missing guest accounts in advance: Entra ID > Users > Invite external user, using the same email address as the original sharing link (needs at least Guest Inviter or User Administrator).

Alternatively, a user with sharing permissions can share or reshare one file, folder or site with the person. That creates the guest account and restores access to everything shared before, so items don't need to be reshared one by one.
Check Entra ID > External Identities > External collaboration settings so the people who share are allowed to invite guests. Assign the Guest Inviter role where needed.
Keep Entra B2B email one-time passcode enabled as the fallback for guests without another sign-in method. It is not being retired.
Compare your SharePoint domain allow/deny lists with the Entra B2B allow/deny list, since the Entra list now applies to SharePoint sharing too.
Warn the help desk: older links can now fail for external partners.
pitfalls: There is no opt-out, you can't choose the date, and the change can't be scoped to individual sites.
Anyone (anonymous) links are not affected.
Guests are now Entra B2B users, so your Conditional Access and MFA policies for guests apply to them, including the SMS and voice retirement.
If an Entra setting is more restrictive than the SharePoint or OneDrive setting, the Entra setting wins.
The retirement covers commercial tenants. Microsoft will announce dates for GCC, GCC High and DoD separately.
done_when: External users on key sites have matching Entra B2B guest accounts.
External collaboration settings let your sharers invite guests, and Entra B2B email one-time passcode is still enabled.
The help desk has been briefed.

title: Catch phishing in Teams chats: ZAP for Teams, QR-code URL detection and user reporting
problem: Since early October 2026 (rollout completes early November), Defender for Office 365 also extracts the URLs hidden in QR codes in Teams messages after delivery and puts a warning on malicious ones. With ZAP for Teams on, eligible malicious internal messages can be blocked.
steps: Microsoft Defender portal > Settings > Email & collaboration > Microsoft Teams protection (security.microsoft.com/securitysettings/teamsProtectionPolicy): check that the Zero-hour auto purge (ZAP) toggle is On.
On the same page, pick the quarantine policies for malware and high-confidence phishing, and add exclusions only if you really need them. Exclusions apply to recipients, not senders.
PowerShell alternative: `Get-TeamsProtectionPolicy | Format-List Name,ZapEnabled` and `Set-TeamsProtectionPolicy -Identity "Teams Protection Policy" -ZapEnabled $true`.

Turn on user reporting in two places: 'Report a security concern' in the Teams admin center messaging policies (plus calling and meeting reporting if you want them), and 'Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams' on the Teams user reported settings page (security.microsoft.com/securitysettings/teamsUserSubmission). Existing tenants need to enable the Defender setting themselves.
Hunt for QR-code detections in Advanced Hunting: `MessageUrlInfo | where UrlLocation == "QRCode"`.
Tell the SOC that users can now also report Teams calls, meetings and meeting participants, so these reports show up on the Submissions page.
pitfalls: ZAP for Teams and Safe Links for Teams need Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 or higher, which Microsoft 365 E3 has included since July 2026. Advanced hunting on Teams messages needs Plan 2 or Microsoft 365 E5.
ZAP for Teams quarantines only internal chats and channels, and only for malware and high-confidence phishing.
Quarantined Teams messages are currently admin-only, and users get no quarantine notifications.
User reporting in Teams isn't supported in GCC, GCC High and DoD.
done_when: `Get-TeamsProtectionPolicy` shows ZapEnabled True.
'Report a security concern' is on in Teams messaging policies and 'Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams' is on in Defender.
The SOC has a saved hunting query for QR-code URLs in Teams.

title: Decide who can create agents in Entra before default users get the right on 4 November 2026
problem: From 4 November 2026 (rollout through late November), users without any Entra role can create agent identity blueprints, and the agents built from them, unless you set 'Users can create agent blueprints' to No.
steps: Sign in to the Entra admin center as at least a Cloud Application Administrator.
Entra ID > Users > User settings > Default user role permissions: set 'Users can create agent blueprints' to No and save. You can do this now; it takes effect when the rollout reaches your tenant.

Give named builders the Agent ID Developer role, which lets them create blueprints and blueprint principals. Reserve Agent ID Administrator for people who must add a secret or certificate to a blueprint.
Review 'Users can register applications' at the same time. The new setting is independent of it.

It doesn't block an app or an agent from creating identities, so review which apps hold Graph permissions for that.
The label may read slightly differently in the portal while the feature rolls out. It is under Default user role permissions.
It doesn't change the requirements in Microsoft Foundry or Security Copilot, such as licenses and Azure subscriptions.

title: Prompt: write a Copilot rollout announcement
problem: You need a clear end-user announcement for Copilot.
steps: Open Microsoft Copilot Chat (formerly Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat) or your approved AI tool.

'Write a 200-word announcement for employees that Microsoft Copilot is being rolled out to [group] on [date]. Include: what it is, 3 concrete use cases for [department], where to get training, and a reminder that Copilot only shows content they already have access to.'
Review the output critically and verify facts against official documentation.
pitfalls: Never paste secrets, tenant IDs or personal data into tools not approved for that data.
AI output can be wrong — treat it as a draft.
done_when: The announcement has been reviewed for accuracy and approved by the owner of internal communications.

'Draft an acceptable use policy for generative AI tools at [company]. Cover: approved tools, data that must not be entered, verifying outputs, sensitivity labels, reporting incidents, and consequences. Keep it under 1 page and in plain language.'
